text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: High error rate detected for service=api-public. 5xx spike across edges; observed Cloudflare 525 / TLS handshake failures and 524 timeouts. Impact: many requests -> 502/524/525. Severity: P1. @oncall alerting.

alice_m: Ack, I’m on call. Seeing a sudden surge in 525s from multiple Cloudflare edge IPs in logs. Origin responses look fine when hit directly from infra.

jon_sre: I can join. Can you paste a sample failure trace? Also check Cloudflare status page and our DNS provider.

alice_m: paste: ```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/health
* About to connect() to api.redwood-inference.com port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 104.21.12.34...
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (104.21.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood-inference.com:443
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood-inference.com:443
```

kari_prod: Support is getting customer reports: EU customers see TLS handshake errors -> failing to establish session. No application-layer errors in our logs when hitting origin directly from us-east-1.

eng-infra-bot: Observability alert: increased RTT and TLS handshake failures starting 2026-03-15T11:05:xxZ. Cloudflare status: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/abcd1234 - DNS and edge routing degraded in US & EU.

support-lead: Tagging major customers: @enterprise-acct-team — they are getting escalations. We should post status brief to status.redwood.com ASAP.

jon_sre: Hypothesis: Cloudflare edge->origin TLS failing due to SNI or ALPN negotiation regression at CF, or intermittent TCP resets from CF edges. Two mitigation paths: 1) ask CF to failover/rollback (but might take time) 2) bypass CDN -> update DNS to point to origin load balancer directly (fast but leaks origin IPs + bypasses WAF/ratelimiting).

alice_m: Agreed. I’m going to quick-check origin certs and TLS config. Our origin certs are valid and cert chain looks fine. No recent cert rotates in last 48h.

ops_tony: I can prepare Route53 change: lower TTL and change A/CNAME to api-origin.elb.internal -> will need runbook sign-off for origin exposure and increase WAF rules at LB.

jon_sre: Also get CF support ticket open and request escalation. Add correlation IDs for failures so CF can map.

alice_m: Opening CF ticket now with examples and traceroutes. Ticket id: CF-98765 (sent to tier2). Attach logs + curl output + tcpdump snippet.

eng-infra-bot: Automated health check: origin latency normal (p95 42ms). Edge errors concentrated on Cloudflare PoPs: ORD, AMS, LHR.

kari_prod: We should prepare customer comms: short note that some customers may see intermittent connectivity and we’re working on a fix. I’ll draft a status message after we pick mitigation.

alice_m: Mitigation decision: roll DNS to origin for short window to restore connectivity while CF works the issue. We’ll set TTL=60, change api.redwood-inference.com CNAME -> origin-direct.redwood-infra.net (not proxied). ops_tony, execute?

ops_tony: On it. Plan: 1) set TTL=60 on api record 2) replace CNAME with origin-direct CNAME 3) monitor error rate and token consumption (bypass will increase egress). 4) revert when CF confirms resolution.

support-lead: Reminder: enable WAF at LB (IP allowlist) for origin-direct to limit blast radius. Also send temporary auth header validation note to SEs.

jon_sre: Runbook note: post change, verify TLS handshake succeeds from multiple regions and run full smoke on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. Also update status page.

ops_tony: Route53 changes pushed at 11:19:12Z. TTL=60, CNAME updated -> origin-direct.redwood-infra.net. Propagation in progress.

alice_m: Monitoring: within ~90s post-change, 525s dropped to near-zero, overall 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 0.8%. Latency p50/p95 increased a bit (CDN offload removed).

eng-infra-bot: Metrics update: traffic back to origin. Error budget improving. Noticeable increase in egress costs and CPU on origin pool. Autoscale triggered +2 nodes.

kari_prod: Status page update drafted and published: "We are experiencing degraded connectivity due to Cloudflare edge TLS and routing disruptions. We have temporarily routed traffic to our origin to restore customer connectivity. Engineers are working with Cloudflare to restore normal CDN routing."

jon_sre: CF replied: root cause under investigation; they confirmed edge certificate handshake anomalies due to config push in multiple PoPs. CF estimates ~2hr to fully remediate and recommends continuing origin fallback. They asked for packet captures.

alice_m: Captures uploaded. Also scheduled on-call handoff in 30m to ops_tony. I’ll leave runbook notes and evidence in the incident tracker.

ops_tony: Taking over on-call at 11:40Z. I’ll continue monitoring rollback window and coordinate with CF.

support-lead: Customer comms: sent proactive emails to 12 enterprise contacts; support queue prioritized. No data loss reported.

jon_sre: Action items recorded: CF ticket + packet captures (CF-98765), DNS fallback applied, WAF at LB enforced, cost/metrics logged. Postmortem required with timeline + mitigation effectiveness + decision rationale.

alice_m: Closing pager for now; keeping channel open for updates. If CF confirms fix, we will gradually revert to CDN after validation (canary per-region).

ops_tony: Confirming steady state at 11:53Z: 5xx < 1%, p95 latency slightly higher but acceptable. Leaving origin route active until CF confirms.

jon_sre: Thanks all. Postmortem owner: @jon_sre. Please add any missing customer escalations.

support-lead: Note for postmortem: include cost delta for bypass window and list customers who contacted support.

eng-infra-bot: Incident state: mitigation in place, monitoring. Next update when CF confirms or when we start canary rollback.

ops_tony: End-handoff note: I’ll keep a watch, escalate if CF asks to revert earlier.

alice_m: Thanks team. Great quick coor.
